svg.title: Discrete switching versus continuous decision space
svg.desc: Interactive chart comparing a hard if/else threshold at 30% HP with continuous intent from XML anchors plus a network delta. Move the pointer, use arrow keys, or toggle the two modes.
svg.text: A threshold is a cliff — a decision space is a slope
Same inputs, same anchors. Toggle between the if/else version and the XML + network delta version.

g.aria-label: Show the continuous XML plus network version

svg.text: Move the pointer over the chart, or use ← → after clicking it.
● markers are the three values quoted in the post (HP = 29% / 31% / 35%): retreat 0.9 / 0.7 / 0.3, attack 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.6, resupply 0.0 / 0.1 / 0.1.
The rest of each curve is interpolated between those anchors — monotone, so it never overshoots or invents a new action.
Red lines still clamp the result: below 10% HP the XML safety layer forces retreat no matter what the network outputs.
